chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, both from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Hariz ibn 'Abdillah, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"There is no harm if the person in ihram disciplines his slave, between him and ten strikes."

key_terms.أَسْوَاطٍ: Strikes (plural of sawt, a whip or strike)
key_terms.اَلْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: What is the limit of disciplining a slave for a person in ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that a muhrim retains the right to discipline their slave, limiting corporal punishment to a maximum of ten strikes to prevent excessive harm. It reflects the juristic consensus on maintaining social hierarchy during the sacred state of ihram, ensuring that ritual restrictions do not nullify domestic authority while preserving justice.
